name: ComMarker Omni X UV
tagline: Desktop UV laser for glass, plastic, and fine detail
tldr: ComMarker Omni X uses UV wavelength for cold marking on glass, some plastics, and delicate materials without as much heat damage as fiber or CO₂. Slower than fiber on metal: different tool for different materials.
mainObjective: Detailed engraving on organics and coated metal: occasional thin cuts only

priceRange.note: Official ComMarker store, Oct 2026: $3,599 to $7,059 depending on 6W or 12W and bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

pros: Class 1 enclosure with OD 5+ shielding, door sensor and safety key: no goggles needed in normal use
ComMarker claims 99.72% dust isolation inside the enclosure, useful when engraving plastics in a shared room
LiDAR autofocus and a 235 mm maximum processing height for tall objects
cons: $300 more than the open-frame Omni XE for the same laser options
32 kg and 515 × 320 × 655 mm: heavier and taller than the Omni XE (20 kg)
From $3,599 for the 6W basic bundle (ComMarker store, Oct 2026), far above diode lasers that also engrave wood and leather

faq.question: Omni X or Omni XE: what is the difference?
faq.answer: Both use the same 355 nm UV source options (6W or 12W), the same 10,000 mm/s galvo, LiDAR autofocus and work areas, according to ComMarker's spec pages. The Omni X is the enclosed version: Class 1 laser safety, OD 5+ shielding, door sensor and safety key, 32 kg. The Omni XE is rated Class 4, weighs 20 kg and costs $300 less. Pick the X if it will run in a shared room, a shop counter or near children.

faq.question: 6W or 12W Omni X?
faq.answer: ComMarker lists the Omni X basic bundle at $3,599 (6W) or $5,999 (12W) in October 2026. The 12W gets a 250 × 250 mm field instead of 150 × 150 mm and more multi-pass cutting capacity: 12 mm basswood, 10 mm acrylic and 1 mm stainless, against 8 mm, 6 mm and 0.6 mm for the 6W. A 12W upgrade kit is also sold separately for $3,499.

faq.question: Can the Omni X mark metal?
faq.answer: Yes: ComMarker lists stainless steel, aluminum, brass, gold and silver, and UV leaves fine, low-heat marks. For deep engraving or high-volume metal work a fiber laser is faster and cheaper per part. The Omni X earns its place on glass, crystal (including 3D internal engraving), plastics and heat-sensitive items.

standoutFeatures.title: Class 1 enclosed UV
standoutFeatures.body: Fully enclosed with OD 5+ shielding, a door sensor that pauses the job and a safety key. It can run in an office, a retail counter or a classroom without separate laser protection for bystanders.

standoutFeatures.title: Contained dust and fumes
standoutFeatures.body: ComMarker claims 99.72% dust isolation inside the enclosure, and an external fume extractor can be connected for filtration. A practical point when engraving plastics, leather or food items indoors.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 6W base version on ComMarker Omni X UV. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: UV on glass: low power test tiles and fixturing matter more than speed. Keep dedicated presets away from fiber jobs. Confirm material compatibility with ComMarker before quoting UV gift lines.
primaryUse: Engraving-first desktop diode for makers who prioritize mark quality over cut speed

editorialDepth.advantages: ComMarker Omni X UV targets glass, films, and heat-sensitive plastics: profitable when you already sell those jobs, not for casual UV experiments.
editorialDepth.limitations: Poor first-laser purchase. No wood or metal cutting. Confirm the module material list before buying the chassis.
